_readme: Jurisdiction registry for the generic open-data connectors (Socrata, ArcGIS).
COVERAGE GROWS BY APPENDING ENTRIES, NEVER BY WRITING CONNECTOR CODE. There is no
jurisdiction-specific logic anywhere in sources/socrata.ts or sources/arcgis.ts — a new
city is one more object in this file. See docs/source-registry.md.
RULES (enforced by the connector + the run report):
• status_to_bucket values are copied VERBATIM from the dataset's live distinct status
values (query SELECT DISTINCT via SoQL first — never guessed). A status not listed in
any bucket is logged in the run report, the record is EXCLUDED, and it never lands in a band.
• coverage is state + county (or state alone for a statewide dataset). The engine filters
to the ZIPs HomeSignal actually serves, so adding a ZIP never touches this file.
• type_map maps a VERBATIM source classification value to one of the six use-types:
Industrial | Development | Residential | Utility | Commercial | Civic/Public.
An unmapped/absent value → use_type:'unclassified' (logged), never inferred from the title.
• record_url: from the column named in column_map.record_url when present (string, or an
object whose .url is used), else record_url_template with {case_number}/{<col>} filled,
else the dataset landing page with record_url_precision:'dataset'.
_arcgis_readme: ArcGIS FeatureServer connector (sources/arcgis.ts) — the Esri twin of the Socrata one.
Same discipline: append an entry here, never edit the connector. An entry needs:
registry_id, platform:'arcgis', service_url (the LAYER query base .../FeatureServer/0),
column_map (read point lat/lng from geometry via the flattened '__lat'/'__lng' columns),
status_to_bucket (VERBATIM live distinct values — query first, never guess),
The ZIP column is MANDATORY. STATUS: connector BUILT + unit-tested + wired (arcgisForZip).
Add verified entries here as clean per-address permit/case FeatureServers are confirmed.
_csv_readme: CSV-file connector (sources/csv.ts) - for first-party portals whose interface is a published
CSV file (first consumer: San Diego's seshat.datasd.org approvals ledger). Same discipline:
append an entry here, never edit the connector. The file is fetched ONCE per cache window
(module memo, cache_minutes default 360) with include_types + recency + column projection
applied at parse time, then every ZIP in the batch is served from the compact cached rows.
ZIP scoping: column_map.zip when the file has one, else spatial_zip_radius_mi (each row's
OWN coords vs the ZIP centroid - a garbage coordinate can never land near a centroid, so
bad source geometry self-excludes). Statuses/types VERBATIM, fail-closed, record_url
column -> template -> dataset landing page. Batches should fire csv-covered ZIPs in modest
waves so cold isolates don't multiply the file download.
_carto_readme: Carto SQL-API connector (sources/carto.ts) - for Carto-hosted open-data portals
(first consumer: Philadelphia's phl.carto.com permits table). Same discipline: append
an entry here, never edit the connector. SQL dialect is PostgreSQL; ZIP scoping is a
LIKE '{zip}%' prefix because Carto portals store ZIP+4; geometry rides PostGIS
(geom_col -> SELECT ST_Y/ST_X AS __lat/__lng - rows place by their OWN parcel point).
Statuses/types VERBATIM, fail-closed, record_url column -> template -> dataset page.

LIVENESS (three-part): name clean; entity = Sussex County DE Planning & Zoning; newest application_rcvd_date 2026-07-27, three days before wiring. STATUS VOCABULARY IS COMPLETE AND VERBATIM: live groupBy on cc_decision returned 16 values summing to EXACTLY 2,566 (positive control), exceededTransferLimit=false. Mapped above verbatim; the connector trims both sides so 'Approved ' folds onto 'Approved'. Deliberately UNMAPPED, fail-closed: null (172) = filed, no Council decision yet, and the value '8/19/2025' (1) = a date typed into the decision field, a publisher data-entry error with no bucketable meaning. Those 173 rows are DROPPED, not guessed. TYPE IS A CONSTANT AND THAT IS THE HONEST CHOICE, NOT A SHORTCUT: proposed_use is the semantically correct column and is FREE TEXT -- 400+ distinct values over 2,566 rows, mostly n=1, with typos ('electrial subsation') and prose ('operate a food truck for a period exceeding three days'). Rule 5 terminal, no type_map exists. current_zoning IS a closed 38-value vocabulary summing to exactly 2,566, and was REJECTED as the type source because it describes the PARCEL, not the PROPOSAL: a conditional use is by definition something the existing zoning does not allow, so AR-1 -> Residential would have labelled an electrical substation 'Residential'. use_type_const 'Development' renders the generic 'Other project' pin and asserts nothing about the use (Phoenix residual-bucket precedent). record_url_precision is 'dataset': the layer carries no per-case URL column and Sussex's case search is not addressable per application_number, so templating one would be guessing. Omitting them is silent: returnGeometry=true is always sent, featurePoint() resolves correctly, and the coordinates are simply never read -- the records still publish, still carry record_url, and still count toward coverage, so nothing fails. Delaware is 29 of PA's 467 dark pages. LIVENESS three-part: NAME clean (Delaware County Subdivisions and Land Developments); DATES recent (Year 2026 = 48 rows, 2025 = 98, and the series runs unbroken 2009-2026 at ~110-140/yr); ENTITY correct (county planning department's own SLD review docket, on the county's own server). STATUS IS A CONST, AND Recommendation WAS REJECTED AS RULE-5 FREE TEXT: it holds ~110 distinct values, overwhelmingly one-off prose with upstream typos ('Disaoproval', 'addressina staff comments', 'plan discreoancies'), and 1,594 of 2,096 rows -- 76% -- literally read 'Please contact Planning Department for Recommendation'. There is no bucketable vocabulary there. status_const 'proposed' is the honest floor: a row means a subdivision or land-development plan was SUBMITTED and reviewed by the county, whose recommendation is advisory while the municipality decides. It does not assert approval, and for 76% of rows the outcome is not published at all. NO file_date, DELIBERATELY -- the source publishes YEAR GRANULARITY ONLY. column_map.file_date is omitted rather than pointed at Year, because isoDay() reads a finite number as EPOCH MILLISECONDS, so Year 2026 would render as 1970-01-01: a precise, confident, wrong date on every record. Mapping year->Jan-1 would be the same fabrication with a friendlier face. A record with no date is honest; a record dated 1970 is not. Recency therefore rides Year in extra_where at a deliberately GENEROUS window (>= 2020, 745 of 2,096 rows) -- coarse, but every row in it is genuinely from that period. DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED AT GO-LIVE, 2026-08-03: the first version set status_const WITHOUT a status_to_bucket, and emitted ZERO records across all 12 probe ZIPs while the source query itself was healthy (19026's 3-mi envelope returns 483 rows unfiltered, 168 with Year >= 2020). Cause: status_const supplies the RAW value, which the connector then resolves through status_to_bucket like any other status (arcgis.ts:300-304) -- with no map, 'proposed' was unmapped, so every row was excluded and flagged. This is the silent-nothing class the Arlington / harris-county-permits notes warn about: config that looks complete, passes every unit test and produces nothing. The detroit-building-permits and cleveland-issued-building-permits convention is the fix -- a self-describing constant that is ALSO a key in the map. Value chosen: 'Submitted for county review', which states exactly what a row means (a plan was submitted and reviewed by the county; its recommendation is advisory and for 76% of rows is not published) rather than the opaque bucket name 'proposed'.

'Development' is a GENERIC_EXACT bucket and therefore NON-TERMINAL, so the downstream keyword rules can still refine 'Demo 17x24 garage' from the title; a terminal guess like Residential could not be refined and would change the pin SHAPE. use_type_const 'Development' catches the ONE row whose Permit_Type is empty (the founder's Adams ruling: an empty publisher field is honest absence, kept under a generic label, not dropped) -- and post-2026-08-03 the constant fills ONLY where the publisher stated nothing. This is the worcester-building-permits class and uses its technique. 2027 IS INCLUDED PREEMPTIVELY so that when the year turns the window widens instead of silently truncating (worcester's receipts warn about exactly this); TRIM/EXTEND THE LIST AT THE ANNUAL DATED-CONSTANT REVIEW. RULE 13 -- PROBED IN THE CONNECTOR'S OWN SCOPE: the exact envelopeFor() math at 3 mi with geometryType=esriGeometryEnvelope, inSR=4326, spatialRel=esriSpatialRelIntersects, plus this entry's own extra_where. Aurora was filterable because its publisher named the trade (Roofing-RT2, Mechanical, Plumbing, Electrical are values IN the type column); Centre's Permit_Type names no trade and does not encode scale, so any filter here would infer scale from a field that does not carry it -- which is guessing, in the one place the anti-fabrication rules exist to stop. || file_date_kind 'issued' — SWEPT AND CONFIRMED 2026-08-09 against the live source, not inferred from the column name. The mapped column `Issue_Date` was verified to exist and to be the issue-dated one, and production confirms it PARSES (the entry emits dates). 2026-08-04 PA/York wire. 47 of 47 pages were dark; the largest single-county lift left in PA after Delaware. Config only. THE EARLIER 'York is a real host that does not answer' WAS THE WRONG HOST: yorkcountypa.gov is the county portal (DNS resolves, then times out at 20s and 60s), while arcweb1.ycpc.org is the York County PLANNING COMMISSION and answers immediately. 'The county's host does not answer' and 'the county publishes nothing' are different claims; only the second is a rejection. THE LAYER DESCRIPTION WOULD HAVE JUSTIFIED A WRONG REJECTION -- it opens 'The Subdivision GIS Layer represents the geographic boundaries...', which reads as a static cadastral layer. The FIELDS say otherwise: it is a plan-review docket (DATE_RCVD, PLAN_TITLE, plan-type and use flags, PROP_LOTS/PROP_DU/PROP_NEW_BLDG_SQFT, MCD, ENGINEER). READ THE SCHEMA, NOT THE BLURB. LIVENESS: 26,884 rows at wire time against 26,879 recorded 2026-08-03 -- the layer grew by 5 in a day, and the 5-year window moved 1,267 -> 1,269 by the same amount. Newest DATE_RCVD 2026-07-27. Names are real and specific (Walmart - Hanover, Fairview South WWTP Expansion, Ballpark Commons). THE DESIGN QUESTION THIS ENTRY SETTLES -- USE IS A SET OF 8 FLAGS, NOT A COLUMN. There is no single use column anywhere in the schema, so type_map cannot key on one value. column_map arrays JOIN with a single space and keep every non-empty part (arcgis.ts readCol), so type_source is the 8 flag columns IN PRECEDENCE ORDER and each key is 8 space-joined YES/NO tokens. This is safe ONLY because the flags are never NULL: probed live, 0 rows in the window have a NULL flag, with a NON-ZERO CONTROL from the same query shape (PLAN_TITLE IS NOT NULL -> 1,269). A NULL would have shortened the joined key and silently missed the map. The flags carry the layer's own BOOLEAN domain (codes YES/NO only), so the key space is closed. PRECEDENCE, STATED ONCE AND APPLIED MECHANICALLY: IND > COM > MF > MHP > SR > AG > SF > OTHER -- the most intensive use wins, and AG OUTRANKS SF (founder ruling, 2026-08-04). The first draft had SF above AG, which rendered the 235-row SF+AG combination -- the SECOND most common in the window -- as Residential. The ruling: a single-family house on agricultural land IS agricultural land being developed; that is the signal a resident wants and the MORE SPECIFIC claim, so the rarer and more consequential fact wins over the commoner one. MEASURED CONSEQUENCE of the re-rank, computed by rebuilding the map under both orders and diffing per COMBINATION (not per key -- the key strings themselves move when the column order changes): EXACTLY 2 of the 32 combinations flip, SF+AG (235) and SF+AG+OTHER (5) = 240 rows, all Residential -> Development, and no other combination moves. Tally 752/226/137/154 -> Residential 512, Commercial 226, Industrial 137, Development 394, 0 unclassified. Note AG maps to 'Development' because the closed use_type set has no agricultural member, so the agricultural signal renders as the generic 'Other project' circle rather than a Residential house -- honest about the ambiguity rather than asserting a housing tract. THIS IS THE ONE JUDGEMENT CALL IN THE ENTRY and it is reversible by editing this map alone -- the 32 keys are measured, the rule is what maps them. ALL 32 COMBINATIONS ARE MEASURED, NOT GUESSED, AND RULE 13 CUT BOTH WAYS HERE: the 5-year window (the one actually wired) holds 32 combinations summing to exactly 1,269, whereas a 3-year probe shows only 29 -- SF+SR, IND+OTHER and MF+SR+OTHER exist ONLY in the wider window. Enumerating at 3 years and wiring at 5 would have dropped those rows to unclassified. An unseen combination still fails closed to unclassified: visible in the count, never a wrong pin. THE ALL-'NO' ROWS NEED AN EXPLICIT KEY, NOT use_type_const. 34 rows in the window set no use flag at all -- honest absence (the founder's Adams ruling), so they render under the generic member. But a joined array yields 'NO NO NO NO NO NO NO NO', which is NOT an empty type_source, so use_type_const would never fire on them. That key is therefore mapped explicitly to 'Development'. AG and OTHER also map to 'Development': the closed use_type set (lib/map.js::TYPE_EXACT) has no agricultural member, and 'Development' is a GENERIC_EXACT bucket -- NON-TERMINAL, so downstream keyword rules can still refine the title, whereas forcing Industrial would be a guess that fixes the pin SHAPE (the chester-county-pa Agricultural precedent). STATUS IS A CONST because the layer has NO status column -- and this CORRECTS the note recorded 2026-08-03 that 'PT_FINAL YES/NO is the closest thing to a lifecycle signal'. It is not: the PT_* flags are themselves a multi-flag set (measured over the same window, 19 combinations summing to exactly 732 at 3y) and 323 rows carry PRELIM+FINAL TOGETHER, so they describe plan TYPE, not stage, and cannot order a lifecycle. Per the delaware-county-pa defect the constant is a SELF-DESCRIBING value that is ALSO A KEY in status_to_bucket -- arcgis status_const is the RAW value resolved through the map, unlike socrata where it IS the bucket. Every row is a plan SUBMITTED to the county for Act 247 review, advisory while the municipality decides; it does not assert approval. Same mechanism and same wording as chester-county-pa-act247-plans next door. GEOMETRY IS POINT (esriGeometryPoint) -- unlike Delaware, Chester and Centre, no centroid derivation is needed; lat/lng read the flattened __lat/__lng (the frisco pattern). SCOPING IS SPATIAL: no ZIP and no address column. TITLE is PLAN_TITLE, 1,269/1,269 populated in the window. MCD was NOT used in the title: it is a coded municipality domain and readCol would emit the raw code ('10'), an opaque value. WINDOW recency_days 1825, matching chester-county-pa-act247-plans -- same Act 247 plan-review mechanism in the adjacent county, and plan review is slow-moving. DATE_RCVD is a real esriFieldTypeDate, so the DATE literal applies directly (no worcester/centre string workaround). RULE 13 -- PROBED IN THE CONNECTOR'S OWN SCOPE (envelopeFor() math at 3 mi, geometryType=esriGeometryEnvelope, inSR=4326, spatialRel=esriSpatialRelIntersects, same DATE literal), WITH NON-ZERO CONTROLS: 17331 Hanover unfiltered 1,868 -> 102 windowed; 17402 York Twp 2,247 -> 111. record_url_precision 'dataset' on the layer's own URL (the worcester precedent): no per-plan public URL was verified, and templating one would be guessing.

_receipts: 2026-08-04 PA/Montgomery wire - the third PA Act 247 entry, after chester-county-pa-act247-plans and york-county-pa-planning-subdivisions, and PA's largest remaining dark block at 62 of 64 pages. Config only. DISCOVERY -- THE HUB IS NOT THE SERVER, AND THIS IS THE SECOND TIME IT PAID (Centre was the first). Montgomery's ArcGIS hub data-montcopa.opendata.arcgis.com returns a DCAT feed whose dataset array is literally empty ([]), which reads as a firm rejection. The county's own SERVER ROOT gis.montcopa.org/arcgis/rest/services carries 19 folders, and Planning/ holds this layer. An empty DCAT dataset array is NOT an empty server - enumerate the server root before recording a rejection. The host was found by SEARCH, not by guessing a hostname. ENTITY CONFIRMED FROM CONTENTS, NOT THE HOSTNAME: the municipalities are Towamencin, Norristown, Plymouth and Lower Merion, all genuinely Montgomery County PA. The cross-state trap here is real and adjacent - opendata-mcgov-gis is Montgomery County MARYLAND, which is ALREADY WIRED as the montgomery-county-* socrata trio; montcopa is the Pennsylvania county. LIVENESS (three-part): name clean; entity = Montgomery County Planning Commission; newest Entry_Date 2026-07-29, six days before wiring, with real specific names (Belfair Square Final Plan Revision, AFM Buildings, 1920 Little Ave, 112 Bryn Mawr Avenue). 7,201 rows layer-wide. STATUS IS A CONST BECAUSE THE LAYER HAS NO STATUS COLUMN, AND THE BUCKET IS proposed BY FOUNDER RULING 2026-08-04 -- DO NOT RE-PROPOSE IT AS approved. Act 247 is the Pennsylvania Municipalities Planning Code provision requiring a municipality to SUBMIT a subdivision or land-development plan to the COUNTY planning commission for REVIEW BEFORE the municipality itself acts. A row is therefore a filing under advisory county review, not an approval, and understating a project's stage is the honest direction. The constant is a SELF-DESCRIBING value that is ALSO A KEY in status_to_bucket -- arcgis status_const is the RAW value resolved through the map (unlike socrata, where it IS the bucket). Wording is deliberately IDENTICAL to chester-county-pa-act247-plans so the three PA Act 247 entries read the same on a page. TYPE IS A CONSTANT AND THAT IS THE HONEST CHOICE, NOT A SHORTCUT -- SAME CONCLUSION AS ALLEGHENY, REACHED THE SAME WAY. Two candidate columns, neither usable. (a) Proposal_Type is a closed 3-value vocabulary that enumerates EXACTLY against the layer total as a positive control -- Plan Only 5,463 + Ordinance Only 301 + Plan and Ordinance 56 + NULL 1,381 = 7,201 -- but it describes the FILING CLASS, not the building use. (b) Land_Use_1 is a closed 19-value vocabulary but every value is an OPAQUE CODE: T, RDE, RAE, RSA, RSD, AG, RE, RM, MUN, INE, RDC, INS, U, RME, PO, IND, C, OS. AG/IND/C/OS/INS are guessable; the EIGHT R-prefixed residential variants (RDE, RAE, RSA, RSD, RDC, RME, RM, RE) cannot be decoded without the county's own legend, and use_type drives the pin SHAPE, so guessing would fix a wrong shape on a real parcel. use_type_const 'Development' renders the generic Other project pin and asserts nothing about the use (Sussex/Weld/Phoenix precedent). FUTURE REFINEMENT, NOT CHASED NOW (founder): if the county publishes a Land_Use legend, this entry can gain a real type_map by editing this entry alone. THE NULL-TYPE PROBLEM DISSOLVES INSIDE THE WINDOW AND THE extra_where GUARD IS WHY. Layer-wide, 1,381 of 7,201 rows carry a NULL Proposal_Type (19%). In the 1,095-day window only 4 do -- the NULLs are almost entirely historical -- and those same 4 rows are exactly the rows with a NULL Proposal_Name and a NULL URL_Documents. Measured: window 817 rows, 813 with a name, 813 with a URL, 817 with an MCPC_Number; and window AND Proposal_Name IS NOT NULL AND Proposal_Type IS NULL returns EXACTLY 0. So the Proposal_Name IS NOT NULL guard drops 4 unusable rows (no name, no document link, no type) and leaves a clean 813. WINDOW RECONCILED TO 1825 -- ALL THREE PA ACT 247 ENTRIES NOW READ IDENTICALLY (founder ruling 2026-08-04, superseding the same day's 1095). Measured named-row counts: 365d 253, 1095d 813, 1825d 1,396. This entry SHIPPED AT 1095 and was reconciled within hours; the flag is left here rather than deleted because the reasoning is the durable part. The first ruling was made before the sibling convention was known: chester-county-pa-act247-plans and york-county-pa-planning-subdivisions both use 1825 on the SAME Act 247 plan-review mechanism, and they shipped first. THREE ENTRIES ON ONE MECHANISM WITH TWO WINDOWS IS DRIFT. 1825 is also the more ACCURATE window, not merely the consistent one: Act 247 plan reviews run multi-year, so a three-year cut truncates live cases mid-review. Worth 583 more rows on Montgomery alone. If a future session finds a reason to narrow any of the three, narrow ALL THREE together or the drift returns. GEOMETRY IS POLYGON and rides the shipped featurePoint() shoelace centroid. return_centroid is deliberately NOT set: this is a classic ArcGIS Server MapServer, which SILENTLY IGNORES the parameter (standing answer - only hosted AGO FeatureServers honour it), so the local derivation is the path and setting it would be a no-op that implies otherwise. column_map lat/lng are __lat/__lng, WITHOUT WHICH EVERY RECORD SILENTLY LANDS ON THE ZIP CENTROID AT scope=area -- the Sussex defect, which publishes and counts normally and is caught only by checking scope on live rows. THE NATIVE SPATIAL REFERENCE IS NOT WGS84 AND THAT WAS VERIFIED, NOT ASSUMED: the layer declares wkid 102729 / latestWkid 2272 (PA State Plane South, feet). The connector requests outSR=4326 and this server honours it -- probed live, returned spatialReference {wkid 4326} with a first vertex [-75.282085, 40.070857], which is Spring Mill Road in Montgomery County PA. Had the server ignored outSR, every centroid would have been a State Plane foot value rendered as a lat/lng. SCOPING IS SPATIAL at 3 mi (the sibling PA convention): there is no ZIP column anywhere in the schema. Entry_Date is a real esriFieldTypeDate, so recency_days' DATE literal applies directly - no worcester/centre string-LIKE workaround and no Anaheim string compare. record_url_precision is 'record': URL_Documents carries a per-record webapp04.montcopa.org/pc247public/spdocument/spdocumentlist/<id> link, and it DISCRIMINATES (the San Diego OpenDSD standing answer - a URL that returns the same shell for any id is dataset precision, not record). Probed live: a real id (108325) returns 5,329 bytes of document listing; a bogus id (99999999) returns 2,178 bytes matching not-found. This is a stronger record_url than either sibling, both of which are dataset-precision. NOTE ON COVERAGE OVERLAP: 19118 and 19128 are physically Philadelphia but modelled under Montgomery by the Census crosswalk (recorded in the PENNSYLVANIA WIRE PASS), so a 3-mile circle from their centroids can legitimately pull Montgomery County filings across the city line. That is real adjacency, not leakage - the records are genuine Montgomery County Act 247 filings within 3 miles of those ZIP centroids.

file_date_kind 'filed' — and NOT the fourth wrong column it was flagged as. VALUE-PROBED 2026-08-09 against the layer's own `Received_Date`, which sits unused beside the `Entry_Date` in service (the TxDOT/MassDOT shape). They are the SAME event: Entry_Date is Received_Date truncated to midnight, on 8 of 8 newest rows — 1785888000000 = 2026-08-05 vs '8/5/2026 1:54:17 PM'; 1785715200000 = 2026-08-03 vs '8/3/2026 6:12:25 PM'; 1785369600000 = 2026-07-30 vs '7/30/2026 12:00:00 AM'; 1785110400000 = 2026-07-27 vs '7/27/2026 3:27:37 PM'. Entry_Date is also the BETTER of the two: esriFieldTypeDate against a String(50) whose values are format-inconsistent (min '01/02/2007', max '9/9/2022 3:09:09 PM' — lexicographic, so that pair is not even a range). Positive control that the column in service is the one being filtered: production's oldest is 2021-08-09 against a recency_days of 1825 from 2026-08-09 = 2021-08-10, and production's newest, 2026-08-05, is the layer's own max. DO NOT REMAP to Received_Date.

arcgis._receipts: 2026-08-05 OH/Summit wire (Akron). Summit was 0 of 41 pages live -- the single largest dark block in Ohio. Config only. ⚠️ SMALL BY DESIGN: this layer holds 16 rows, so the honest expectation is a modest page lift, not a metro-scale one. It is wired because 16 real, dated, per-parcel filings are 16 real filings (the Weld/Chester precedent), not because it fills the county. DISCOVERY -- THE HOST WAS DERIVED FROM THE HUB'S OWN DATASET URLs, NEVER GUESSED. Summit's hub data-summitgis.opendata.arcgis.com publishes 138 datasets; extracting the accessURL hosts from its DCAT gave the two REAL Summit-Ohio hosts, scgis.summitoh.net (12 datasets) and the AGO org services3.arcgis.com/3Ukh5HzAdI6WZ3KP (124). ⚠️ CROSS-STATE TRAP, LIVE AND ADJACENT: a plain search for 'Summit County GIS' returns summitcountyco.gov and summitcountypropertyappraiser.org, which are NOT Ohio; maps.summitcounty.org is a live ArcGIS server carrying only parcel viewers and is also NOT confirmed Ohio. Summit OHIO is summitoh.net -- confirmed by co.summitoh.net and permitsearch.summitoh.net. Entity here is further confirmed from CONTENTS: the townships in the data are Sagamore, Copley, Springfield and Richfield, all Summit County OH. FULLY ENUMERATED BEFORE WIRING, ON EVERY SURFACE: the hub's 138 datasets keyword-scanned (only 'Assessed Subdivisions', a cadastral layer, matched); scgis.summitoh.net's SERVER ROOT (16 folders, ~100 root services); and every promising folder -- Admin_and_Planning (County_Council, eSIDs, Zoning only), DOSSS, Hosted (911/heat maps/floodplains/ParcelDrafter/Plats_Legacy). ⚠️ THE 'tyler' FOLDER IS EMPTY -- 0 services, 0 folders. Tyler is the EnerGov permitting vendor, so the folder NAME promises a permit system and delivers nothing; this is the second empty vendor-named folder found (Allegheny's 'Accela' was the first). A vendor name in a folder listing is not a source. permitsearch.summitoh.net is a Bootstrap HTML app with no exposed API. THE LAYER CHOICE IS LOAD-BEARING -- LAYER 2, NOT LAYER 0. The FeatureServer has three layers: 0 Point (24 rows), 1 Line (0 rows, EMPTY), 2 Polygon (16 rows). Layer 0 is NOT development: its rows are county-wide zoning ORDINANCE TEXT amendments -- 'Definitions: RVs', 'Short Term Rentals', 'OH HB 361 Second Discussion', 'Residential and PUD Districts', all ItemType 'Text'. Those are legislative policy items with a nominal point, and publishing them as per-parcel development records would misrepresent them. Layer 2 is the real per-parcel docket: 'Heartridge Subdivision Phase 3 Final Plat' (Sagamore), '790 S. Cleveland Massillon Road' Rezoning (Copley), 'Picton Parkway' Preliminary (Springfield), 'Kaczmar Subdivision' (Richfield). READ THE ROWS, NOT THE SERVICE NAME. VOCABULARIES ARE COMPLETE BY EXHAUSTION, NOT BY SAMPLE -- all 16 rows were pulled in one query, so these ARE the population: ItemType Rezoning 8 + Receipt 2 + null 2 + Final 2 + Riparian 1 + Preliminary 1 = 16; SCPCRec Approve 12 + Table 2 + Other 1 + null 1 = 16; BusinessType New 14 + Old 2 = 16. ItemNumber 16/16 and MeetingDate 16/16 populated. STATUS IS A CONST AND SCPCRec WAS DELIBERATELY REJECTED AS THE STATUS SOURCE. SCPCRec is the commission's RECOMMENDATION, not a decision: the Summit County Planning Commission is ADVISORY to the townships under Ohio law (ORC 303 zoning / ORC 711 plats), exactly the mechanism PA Act 247 encodes. Mapping SCPCRec 'Approve' (12 of 16) to the approved bucket would assert that a project is approved when the township that actually decides has not acted. Same founder ruling as the three PA Act 247 entries, and the constant uses the IDENTICAL wording so all four read the same on a page. TYPE IS A CONST for the same reason as Montgomery PA and Allegheny: ItemType is a FILING CLASS (Rezoning/Final/Preliminary/Receipt/Riparian), not a building use, and there is no use column anywhere in the schema. use_type_const 'Development' renders the generic Other project pin and asserts nothing. GEOMETRY IS POLYGON and rides the shipped featurePoint() shoelace centroid; column_map lat/lng are __lat/__lng, without which every record silently lands on the ZIP centroid at scope=area (the Sussex defect). return_centroid is NOT set: this IS a hosted AGO FeatureServer and would honour it, but the shoelace derivation is already proven equivalent to ~2.9 m and the standing answer is that return_centroid is opt-in per entry, never inferred. SCOPING IS SPATIAL at 3 mi -- no ZIP and no address column exists. MeetingDate is a real esriFieldTypeDate so recency_days' DATE literal applies directly. recency_days 1825 matches the three PA Act 247 entries (reconciled 2026-08-04) -- same advisory-review mechanism, same slow-moving cadence; all 16 rows fall inside it, verified live. record_url_precision 'dataset': the schema carries NO url column of any kind, and no per-item public URL was found, so templating one would be guessing; the county Planning & GIS page was live-verified 200 (40 KB). COVERAGE LIMIT, STATED PLAINLY: the county commission reviews UNINCORPORATED TOWNSHIPS. Akron and the incorporated cities run their own planning departments and are NOT in this layer, so Summit pages over incorporated areas will stay dark on this source. That is a real coverage boundary, not a defect, and it must not be described as county-wide coverage.

2026-08-05 MISSOURI PASS. St. Louis County was 0 of 63 pages live -- the LARGEST single dark county block encountered in any state. Config only. The county's subdivision plat docket: 42 rows, and it is the ONLY St. Louis source found that carries dates at all. QUALITY IS THE REASON IT WAS CHOSEN OVER BIGGER LAYERS: 42/42 rows carry geometry, 42/42 carry DATESUBMIT, 42/42 carry PROP_ADD, PROP_ZIP and MUNICIPALI, and PLATTYPEDE is complete and sums to EXACTLY 42 (Boundary Adjustment 22 / Preliminary 13 / Record 6 / Major Land Disturbance 1). Native PROP_ZIP is used rather than spatial scoping -- the page count is then EXACT rather than a 3-mi estimate: 18 distinct ZIPs (63129 x8, 63128 x5, 63123 x4, 63125 x4, 63138 x3, 63026 x3, 63031/63034/63121 x2, and nine singletons), summing to 42. Measured both ways before choosing: native ZIP lights 18 of the 63 dark pages, a 3-mi spatial scope would light 33. Native ZIP wins on the standing convention that a real ZIP column is exact where a radius is an estimate (the Allegheny note). STATUS COMES FROM PLATTYPEDE, WHICH IS THE SOURCE'S OWN LIFECYCLE LANGUAGE, not a guess: Preliminary is a plat under county review -> proposed; Record (the recorded plat), Boundary Adjustment (a recorded lot-line change) and Major Land Disturbance (an issued grading permit) are all completed county actions -> approved. use_type_const 'Development' because PLATTYPEDE is a FILING CLASS, not a building use, and no use column exists anywhere in the 90-field schema. STALE, STATED PLAINLY: DATESUBMIT spans 2025-01-03 to 2025-12-18 and a direct query for DATESUBMIT >= 2026-01-01 returns EXACTLY 0 -- a calendar-2025 docket that has not rolled over in eight months. Wired under the founder's rule that a stale-but-dated, geolocated, per-record source is wired with its span stated, because understating is the honest direction; it can be windowed, can age out, and can be reprobed, which is what separates STALE from NO_TEMPORAL_FIELD. No recency_days is set: at 42 rows there is no size pressure and a window would only discard the recorded plats that ARE the operating tier (the Dayton reasoning). THE APPARENT SUCCESSORS WERE CHASED AND ARE NOT ONE: 'St. Louis County Subdivisions' (modified 2026-07-22) and 'St. Louis County Subdivisions_3_Draft' (2026-07-28) are WEB MAPS, and both point at SubdivisionTrustees_v2 -- HOA trustee REGISTRATION, a different record class entirely. 'Subdivisions_2025' is a Layer Package, not an endpoint. There is no 2026 successor service. REPROBE CONDITION: if a Subdivisions2026 (or equivalent) service appears, re-point this entry; if none appears by the next annual cycle, re-evaluate as STALE. COVERAGE CEILING, STATED PLAINLY: MUNICIPALI reads UNINCORPORATED on all 42 of 42 rows. St. Louis County contains roughly 90 incorporated municipalities that run their own planning departments and are NOT in this layer, so 18 pages is the ceiling for this source and it must never be described as county-wide coverage. Same shape as the Summit County OH limit. WHAT ELSE WAS ENUMERATED AND REJECTED IN ST. LOUIS COUNTY (org w657bnjzrjguNyOy, 2,502 items, 685 feature services, plus the county's own maps.stlouisco.com/hosting/rest server, all six folders): (a) AGS_ZoningPetitions / Zoning_Petitions -- 3,945 rows and by far the biggest layer, REJECTED NO_TEMPORAL_FIELD: count(last_edited_date) = 0 of 3,945 and max = null, the only date-typed field in the schema empty across the whole table. Its PROCEDURE_ vocabulary is also opaque AND dirty -- 2,441 blank (62%), then PEU 833 / CUP 589 / RDD 22 / SBP 12, with petition numbers leaking into the procedure column (32-15, 44-25, 17-12, 26-21) and stray ' A', ' B', ' C', ' D', R1, R2, R4. (b) Active_Construction_Points (4 rows) and _Lines (29) -- REJECTED NO_TEMPORAL_FIELD, identical 6-field schema (CountyID, Name, Status, URL) with no date field of any kind. Note both 404'd on layer 0: the service sets preserveLayerIds true and the real ids are 101 and 100 -- and those 404s arrived as HTTP 200 carrying an error object, the '200 is not verification' pattern. (c) The Accela FOLDER on the county server holds ONLY Accela_Parcels -- the FOURTH consecutive vendor-named folder that is not a permit source (Summit 'tyler' empty, Allegheny 'Accela' empty, Dayton 'Accela' full of housing code-enforcement, this one full of parcels). THE 1825-DAY WINDOW IS LOAD-BEARING AND IT SOLVES THE ONE REAL PROBLEM. Unwindowed, STATUS is 26 values summing exactly to 23,166 but dominated by 'Closed' at 16,370 (71%) -- a terminal state whose OUTCOME is not recorded, so it can support neither an approved nor an operating claim. Inside 1825 days the layer is 2,675 rows and 'Closed' DISAPPEARS ENTIRELY: the windowed vocabulary is 17 values summing exactly to 2,675 (Approved Subject to Conditions 1007 / Approved 836 / Under Review 141 / Voided 113 / Dismissed 106 / Denied 105 / Recorded 93 / Review on Hold 62 / Cancelled - Customer 55 / Inactive 44 / Expired 38 / To Council 35 / Continued off-Docket 25 / To CPC 10 / To BZA 3 / Revoked 1 / '4' 1). Every one of those is self-describing except the single opaque numeric '4', which is left UNMAPPED and fails closed. The window is the standing 1825 default and is independently the correct choice here. 'Closed' IS NEVERTHELESS MAPPED -- TO exclude, DELIBERATELY. It cannot appear in today's window, but the window MOVES: a case filed in 2024 and closed in 2027 will be both in-window and Closed. Rather than leave that to fail closed silently later, it is mapped to exclude now, because 'Closed' alone asserts neither that a project was approved nor that it was built, and asserting either would be a guess about outcome. The other terminal states (Voided, Dismissed, Denied, Cancelled/Canceled - Customer, Inactive, Expired, Revoked) are excluded for the same reason. Statuses that can only appear outside the current window (Proposed, Pending, Accepted, Released) are mapped anyway so the entry stays correct as the window advances. use_type_const 'Development' because PLANTYPE IS UNUSABLE AS A VOCABULARY: 17,447 of 23,166 are NULL (75%), and the non-null tail is contaminated with individual case identifiers and free text -- 'CLD-FnPlat-2022-00046', 'CD-CPC-2023-00051', 'Jones Iron & Metal - Alley Vacation', 'Rezoning from R-0.5 to R-0.75', 'Somerbrook 7th Plat, Final Plat', 'Final Plat - The Preserve, 8th Plat'. THE DATE QUESTION IS THE WHOLE DECISION, AND IT IS NOT NO_TEMPORAL_FIELD. The obvious timing field, `start`, is a SEASON STRING -- its seven values are Spring 2024 / Summer 2024 / Spring 2025 / Summer 2025 / Fall 2025 / Spring 2026 / Summer 2026, populated 70 of 70 but unparseable by any date literal, the Anaheim/Program_Year class. That is an honest file_date meaning 'when this project entered the 2026 construction program', and it is the UDOT precedent exactly (created_dt chosen on live non-null counts). A layer with a fully-populated real date field is NOT the seventh disqualifier; NO_TEMPORAL_FIELD means there are NO dates, and here there is one on every row. STATUS IS A CONST IN THE SOURCE'S OWN LANGUAGE: there is no status column, and the honest statement is membership of the published program, so status_const is 'In the 2026 county construction program' -> approved (funded and scheduled, not asserted complete). Understating is the honest direction. use_type_const 'Roads & Infrastructure' -- a verified member of the CLOSED lib/map.js TYPE_EXACT vocabulary (it maps to cat('infrastructure')), checked in the file rather than assumed. Neither candidate type column is usable: `Scope` is free text (70/70 populated but groupBy returns nothing enumerable) and `travel` is traffic-impact prose with bare URLs mixed into the values ('Lane Closures, Lane Restrictions' 59, but also 'Please see https://www.ccdotholdorchardroad.com/'). record_url_precision 'dataset': `travel` carries a URL on a handful of rows but is a mixed traffic-impact field, not a per-record link column, so templating one would be guessing. ANNUAL SERVICES ARE SEPARATE PROGRAMS, NOT A UNION AND ITS PARTS. Cook publishes DOTH Construction Projects 2024, 2025 (service PrjLine2025) and 2026 as three distinct services. Only 2026 is wired -- the current program. They are not a superset/subset pair, so the union rule does not apply; wiring the older two would add historical road work, which is a separate decision. Municipal street work by Cook's 130+ suburbs is not in this layer, and the city of Chicago's own work is not either. 78 pages is what a county road program reaches, not county-wide development coverage. || DATE MAPPING DROPPED 2026-08-09: file_date was 'CreationDate', the ArcGIS ROW-CREATION system field — production showed all 403 records inside a single 10-week band (2026-04-14 to 2026-06-25), a GIS load batch rather than a construction schedule. ⚠️ CORRECTION TO THIS AUDIT'S OWN §Q FLAG: 'start' was named as the better column and it is NOT usable — a live probe returned 'Fall 2025' / 'Summer 2026', SEASON STRINGS that isoDay() cannot parse. SCOPE: CT had 288 modelled ZIP pages, 19 lit (hartford-building-permits 9, stamford-major-developments 10) and 269 dark, with SIX of its eight counties at zero.

Its predicate is `AdDate > CURRENT_TIMESTAMP`, and its file_date is AdDate. 2026-08-05 WASHINGTON pass. Statewide coverage with no county (the UDOT precedent). Found via the WSDOT hub DCAT: 467 datasets enumerated, 10 project-titled, of which 'Project Delivery Plan Current' is the only one that is not a frozen year snapshot (2018-2023 are separate archived layers). *** THE LAYER PUBLISHES NO STATUS COLUMN, AND THE OBVIOUS WORKAROUND WOULD HAVE FABRICATED 586 COMPLETIONS. The tempting single-entry design was extra_where 'OperComplete IS NOT NULL' with status_const 'Operationally Complete' -> operating, on the reading that a populated completion date means the project is complete. Cost: three fetches per WA page instead of one, bounded at ~20 records each. arcgis._receipts: 2026-08-05 ARIZONA pass. ADOT's own hosted AGO layer (org clPWQMwZfdWn4MQZ, the org that publishes ADOT's HPMS data on AZGeo), lyrTIPAdoptions_Final2630_view layer 0 'TIPAdoptions' - the ADOPTED FY2026-2030 Transportation Improvement Program. 247 rows, esriGeometryPolyline, statewide coverage with no county (the UDOT precedent). DISCOVERY: ADOT has no hub domain - azdot-adot and gisdata-azdot .opendata.arcgis.com both return 'Domain record(s) not found', and gis.azdot.gov answers but 404s every REST path (a server-issued 404 means the host is alive and the path is wrong, NOT a dead source). The route in was the AZGeo state clearinghouse DCAT (azgeo-open-data-agic.hub.arcgis.com, 1,296 datasets, 23 project-titled) -> ADOT publishes there -> enumerate that org's 886 services. *** THE OBVIOUS CANDIDATE WAS THE WRONG ONE. 'ADOTProjects_AZGEO' is named exactly like the thing we want and is REJECTED: its serviceDescription is literally 'ADOT Projects DRAFT', it holds only 57 centroids, and its Status column is FREE-TEXT PROSE - the most common value is the unedited template placeholder '<Delete this text and enter an explanation for the AR or BS status.>' (4 rows), the rest are project-manager notes dated 2023 ('NTP issued 5/4/23'). So this is a SELF-HOSTED host and section 0 applies in full — a pg_net 200 proves POSTGRES egress, not that the Deno edge runtime can reach it. The Dayton precedent (dayton-oh-capital-improvement-projects, #594, reverted in #595 after 'Connection reset by peer' at Connect on 4 of 4 ZIPs) is the same class and the same state. THE FIRST POST-DEPLOY RE-CACHE IS THE DEPLOY VERIFICATION for this entry: read arcgis_reports[].fetched/emitted, never counts, and REMOVE the entry if the edge cannot connect. arcgis._receipts: 2026-08-12 NY statewide wire. NY was 233/764 record-backed — 531 dark pages, the largest single gap in any state. DISCOVERY: NYSDOT does not publish projects on ArcGIS Online (a 594-result AGO search returns MPOs, counties, consultants and survey123 forms, no NYSDOT project service) and its portal is NOT at the /arcgis/ path a host guess would try — gis.dot.ny.gov/arcgis/rest/services 404s. The real portal is /hostingny/, recovered from the service URLs of third-party AGO items that reference NYSDOT layers (columbiacounty1's NYSDOT Structures items). Root gisportalny.dot.ny.gov/hostingny/rest/services (gis.dot.ny.gov/hostingny mirrors it byte-for-byte) enumerates folders Agile, Asset, Environmental, Framework, Geocortex, Hosted, HWP, Maintenance, Projects, Roadways, Safety, Utilities. HWP holds only ExportImage[GPServer]. LAYER: Projects/CapitalProgramProjects/FeatureServer/0 'Project Points', esriGeometryPoint, 2,487 rows. REJECTED ALONGSIDE, with receipts, so neither is re-probed: (1) data.ny.gov 'Transportation Projects in Your Neighborhood' (rz8t-4kmq, 1,937 rows) is the obvious candidate BY NAME and fails NO_GEOGRAPHY outright — its full column list carries no lat, no lng, no ZIP and no address, only a 'region' ('10 LONG ISLAND') and county names buried in prose; same class as the NJ DCA rejection. (2) The NYS Thruway Authority capital-project sets (f9da-b8zj and siblings) are likewise coordinate-less and their active set samples a 2012 project. LAYER CHOICE — ONE LAYER ONLY, DELIBERATELY: the service exposes three point layers and three polygon layers all named 'Project Points'/'Project Polygons'. They are NOT duplicates of each other — PIN 581606 returns 4 rows on layer 0 and 0 rows on layers 1 and 2 — but their relationship is undocumented and layer1+layer2 (1,759+857=2,616) exceeds layer 0 (2,487), so wiring more than one risks the houston-plat-applications double-emit. Layer 0 is wired alone; layers 1-5 are left for a later pass. Note PIN is NOT unique (4 rows share 581606); the engine's dedup identity includes lat/lng so distinct sites survive as distinct records. TYPE — WORK_CATEGORY, self-describing. groupBy returns 12 values summing to EXACTLY 2,487, the layer row count and therefore the positive control: Corrective Maint 462, BRIDGE PRESERVATION 458, PAVEMENT RECONSTRUCTION 346, OTHER 265, SAFETY 259, BRIDGE REHABILITATION OR REPLACEMENT 254, Preventative Maint 208, PAVEMENT PRESERVATION 95, Renewal 87, Rehabilitation 39, MOBILITY 13, and 1 NULL. All 11 non-null values are mapped; the single NULL row renders unclassified, which is cosmetic under Rule 2. All map to Utility (the txdot/nvdot/okdot/idot/odot precedent) except 'OTHER' (265 rows), which names no specific work and takes the generic member 'Development'. ⚠️ RULE 4 STAGE 2 IS UNAVAILABLE ON THIS SERVER, AND THAT IS RECORDED RATHER THAN GLOSSED: returnDistinctValues returns {'error':'Unable to complete operation.'} on this layer, so the verbatim-casing confirmation Rule 4 prescribes cannot be run. The obvious substitute ALSO fails — the server's where-clause comparison is CASE-INSENSITIVE, proven both ways: WORK_CATEGORY='BRIDGE PRESERVATION' and ='Bridge Preservation' both return 458, and ='Corrective Maint' and ='CORRECTIVE MAINT' both return 462. So the mixed casing visible in the vocabulary (SHOUTING vs Title Case, which is what makes this a real Rule 4 case) cannot be confirmed byte-exact by any method this endpoint offers. WHY THAT IS TOLERABLE HERE, SPECIFICALLY: the connector normalises type_map keys with trim + case-fold (buildTypeLookup), so a casing mismatch cannot cause a miss; and type is COSMETIC under Rule 2 — an unmapped type degrades pin shape, it never drops a record. The casing risk would NOT be tolerable on a status map, where a miss is record loss under Rule 1 — and this entry has no status column to expose that. STATUS — no status field exists in the layer, so status_const supplies it, mapped through status_to_bucket because in arcgis.ts the constant is the RAW VALUE: proposed ['Capital Program']. 'Capital Program' is the publisher's own term (the service is CapitalProgramProjects) and is used rather than the bucket name 'proposed' because test/status-const-must-be-mapped.test.mjs ratchets against bucket-named constants. THE proposed BUCKET IS EVIDENCE-BACKED, NOT ASSUMED: ConstructionCompleteDate is in the FUTURE on 2,486 of 2,487 rows, in the past on 1, and NULL on 0 — this layer is forward-looking planned work almost in its entirety. DATE — DELIBERATELY UNMAPPED. The only date is ConstructionCompleteDate, a PLANNED COMPLETION date, which is not a filing, award or issuance event and does not fit any file_date_kind. Mapping a future completion date as file_date would misdate every record. Undated is correct, as founder-ruled for butler-county-ks-permits and applied to okdot-workplan-roadways and the idot pair. RECORD URL: WEPIURL is genuinely per-record (piyn.dot.ny.gov/PublicPIYN/ProjectDetails?pin=<PIN>), so record_url_precision is 'record'. HOST: gisportalny.dot.ny.gov is SELF-HOSTED, so governance section 0 applies exactly as it did for Ohio's TIMS — a pg_net 200 is not proof the Deno edge runtime can connect. THE FIRST POST-DEPLOY RE-CACHE IS THE VERIFICATION: read arcgis_reports[].fetched/emitted, and if the edge cannot connect, REMOVE the entry (the Dayton precedent), do not leave it declaring coverage it cannot serve. spatial_zip_radius_mi 3: no ZIP column, matching txdot/okdot/idot/odot.

arcgis._receipts: 2026-08-13 NEW HAMPSHIRE WIRE (QUEUE zero-states item; NH was 0/247, the largest state at literal zero). ROW FILTER IS THE PUBLISHER'S OWN: the web map carries definitionExpression "IS_TEN_YEAR = 'YES'", so extra_where reproduces exactly what NHDOT displays on its public Ten Year Plan map -- 340 of the layer's 6,913 rows. Including Completed follows ctdot-project-work-areas ('06_Completed' -> operating) and wsdot-project-delivery-plan-complete. TYPE: there is NO work-category column (SPECIAL_CODE is null on the sampled rows; PRIMARY_TIER is a road tier integer), so use_type_const 'Utility' -- the same honest-absence choice as mdot-stip, nj-stip, maine-dot, iowa-dot, vtrans, ctdot, aldot, wsdot, adot, wisdot, akdot and hdot. arcgis._receipts: ⚠️ THREE-WAY ACRONYM COLLISION — READ BEFORE ASSUMING A STATE. NDOT = NEBRASKA Department of Transportation (this entry, registry_id "ndot-*", coverage NE). NVDOT = NEVADA (registry_id "nvdot-*", coverage NV) — note Nevada's agency ALSO self-abbreviates NDOT, which is why that entry's own receipts say "NDOT's own ArcGIS Server" while meaning Nevada. NDDOT = NORTH DAKOTA, which is a DIFFERENT agency and is NOT wired by this entry or any other. A session skimming for "ND" can read this row as North Dakota and wrongly conclude that state is covered; North Dakota carried 152 dark ZIP pages when this note was added (2026-08-24). [VERIFIED 2026-08-15 via pg_net against the live endpoint, in the connector's own scope] NDOT's Program Book (segment register). Nebraska was a county-only state at 138 dark of 174 ZIP pages (20.7% live). ⚠️ CROSS-STATE ACRONYM COLLISION - THE MOST DANGEROUS FINDING HERE, AND IT LOOKS HEALTHY IF MISSED: ndot.maps.arcgis.com is **NEVADA** Department of Transportation (id 9Y4hSlLf13E9S0Eo, urlKey NDOT, access public) - a LIVE PUBLIC ORG for the WRONG STATE, and Nevada is already wired here as nvdot-project-boundaries. Wiring from it would have published Nevada roadwork on Nebraska ZIP pages with clean invariants and a plausible count, ~1,200 miles wrong. The `_ndor` owner suffix is ALSO Nevada (jsekanovich_ndor = Nevada Division of Outdoor Recreation, OHV grants/trails). Nebraska's own NDOR account (munn_ndor, Nebraska Dept of Roads, the pre-2017 name) holds only 4 Grant-Portal items from 2024-10-03 - not projects. Same class as the Michigan recon's `Kent` hits resolving to Delaware and Rhode Island, but with a live public org behind it. **Confirm the ORG NAME, never the acronym.** SERVER PATH WAS THE BLOCKER FOR THE SIXTH STATE RUNNING: maps.dot.nebraska.gov fails DNS; gis.ne.gov/portal returns HTTP 500 'Application Error'; gis.ne.gov/arcgis 404s; dot-nebraska.opendata.arcgis.com does not exist. The live path is **gis.ne.gov/dot/rest/services/**, found by resolving nebraska.maps.arcgis.com -> org 'State of Nebraska' (Sj9eBhzWwOMzQCfI, urlKey nebraska, access PUBLIC), then an orgid-scoped search that surfaced ProgramBook_NDOT and reading the item's own url field. Eight dead ends preceded the live one. ⚠️ POINTS AND SEGMENTS ARE **NOT** DISJOINT - THIS IS THE HOUSTON-PLAT CASE, NOT THE MINNESOTA CASE. The service has two layers with IDENTICAL field sets: 0 'Program Book Points' (337 rows, esriGeometryPoint) and 1 'Program Book Segments' (558 rows, esriGeometryPolyline). Measured live by pulling every ProjectNo from BOTH and comparing: Points carry 130 distinct ProjectNo, Segments 437, and **28 ProjectNo values appear in BOTH**. Wiring both entries would double-emit those 28 projects on every page, which exact-identity dedup CANNOT catch across two source_registry_ids. Only the SEGMENT layer is wired (larger: 558 rows / 437 distinct projects). **ACCEPTED COST, STATED PLAINLY: the 102 ProjectNo values unique to the POINTS layer are NOT represented.** The obvious fix - an extra_where excluding the 28 shared numbers - was REJECTED because it means hand-transcribing a 28-item list into config, the founder rule against transcribing a list rather than computing it. Compare mndot-stip/chip-roadway-projects, where groupBy Fiscal_Yea proved a TRUE partition (zero overlap) and two entries were therefore safe. **Identical schemas in one service prove nothing either way - run the id-overlap test.** NO STATUS COLUMN (fields: ProjectName, ProjectNo, ControlNo, County, District, Hwy, BeginRP, EndRP, Length, Estimate, ProgramYear, TypeImprovement, ID_1year) so status_const is used - the detroit-building-permits pattern, and 'Programmed' describes the record rather than restating a bucket (the ratchet in status-const-must-be-mapped.test.mjs, which caught the Minnesota draft). **IT MAPS TO `proposed`, DELIBERATELY THE CONSERVATIVE DIRECTION.** ProgramYear on the segment layer is '2027' (87) and '2028-2032' (the remainder); on the point layer '2027' 76 + '2028-2032' 261 = 337 exactly. The large majority is future-year programming, so mapping the whole register to `approved` would overstate what NDOT has committed to. `proposed` understates at worst - fail-closed in spirit. NO file_date: ProgramYear is a STRING and one of its two values is the RANGE '2028-2032', not a date or even a single year - unusable as a date and never fabricated into one. recency_days absent for the same reason. 18 pre-existing entries already omit file_date, including modot-stip-locations-accepted and scdot-project-viewer-lines. COLUMN POPULATION VERIFIED ON THE WIRED LAYER BEFORE MAPPING (the arlington/harris-county-permits failure class): ProjectName IS NULL -> 0, ProjectNo IS NULL -> 0, Hwy IS NULL -> 0. Real sampled rows: 'Giltner East' / NH-80-7(176) / Hwy 080 / Hamilton / 'Crack Seal'; 'Jct N-13 - Jct N-98' / NH-81-4(131) / Pierce / 'Mill, Resurf.'; 'Niobrara East & West' / S-12-5(1011) / Knox. Every string column is heavily RIGHT-PADDED upstream (char columns); the connector trims both sides - the harris-county-plats precedent. address maps Hwy ALONE, not [Hwy, County] - column_map arrays JOIN their values, they do NOT fall back (the UDOT standing answer). use_type_const 'Utility' rather than a TypeImprovement map: every value is highway/bridge/traffic infrastructure (Br. 76, Intersection 39, Cameras & RWIS 34, DMS Retrofit 24, Closure Signs 21 ...) and use_type is a CLOSED six-value vocabulary (lib/map.js::TYPE_EXACT). record_url_precision 'dataset': no per-record URL column (Boulder/Philadelphia precedent). spatial_zip_radius_mi 3: no ZIP column; records place by their OWN polyline-derived point via featurePoint(). ⚠️ RISK: every probe is pg_net; edge-runtime reachability of gis.ne.gov is UNVERIFIED until the post-deploy smoke - and note gis.ne.gov/portal already 500s, so this host is not uniformly healthy. _receipts.gap: The geometry sibling of the already-wired ndot-program-book-segments (layer 1). This service has exactly two layers — 0 "Program Book Points" (337 rows) and 1 "Program Book Segments" (558 rows) — and only layer 1 was ever wired. Same shape as the Montana MDT gap, but where MT layer 0 held only 5 rows this one holds 337.
_receipts.overlap: Measured on COMPLETE ProjectNo sets via groupByFieldsForStatistics, each summing EXACTLY to its layer row count (337 and 558), so complete rather than sampled. L0 130 distinct ProjectNo, L1 437, sharing 28. Wiring L0 therefore adds 102 projects that exist nowhere else and would DOUBLE-EMIT 28 without a yield.
_receipts.yield_rationale: POINTS yields_to SEGMENTS on the 28 shared ProjectNo. A polyline intersects many ZIP radii where a point sits in exactly one, so the segment is the copy worth keeping. Same class as ID/WY/OH/ME/VT/UT/IA/VA/SD; the NY layer set is the counter-case where declaring a yield would DROP records. Measured per source, never inherited. NOTE: ProjectNo is right-padded upstream ("STP-283-2(108)             ") — the yield hook compares on TRIMMED string equality, which is what makes the match survive the padding.
_receipts.status: No status column exists on either layer, so status_const "Programmed" bucketed proposed — matching the wired sibling exactly. That bucket is PROVABLE here rather than assumed: ProgramYear is a complete 2-value vocabulary summing exactly to 337 and both values are FUTURE — "2027" (76) and "2028-2032" (261) — as of 2026-08-24. This is the Idaho ITIP situation, NOT the Wyoming one where drft_year spanned 2020-2032 and forced a forward window.
_receipts.no_date_field: There is no esriFieldTypeDate field. ProgramYear is a String that holds a RANGE ("2028-2032") as well as single years, so it is not a date and is not mapped as one. file_date / file_date_kind / recency_days are therefore absent — the shape 33 other programmed-work entries already use.
_receipts.use_type: use_type_const "Utility", matching the wired sibling. TypeImprovement was enumerated complete (47 values summing exactly to 337) and deliberately NOT mapped: it is free-text with publisher typos and near-duplicates ("Br" vs "Br.", "Resurf, Br" vs "Resurf. Br", "Mill, Rusurf." vs "Mill, Resurf."), and mapping it on ONE layer while the sibling uses a flat const would make the same project render as a different use_type depending on which geometry it was published in.
_receipts.coverage_note: County spans Nebraska statewide, so coverage declares {state: NE} with no county, matching the sibling and the UDOT statewide precedent. NE carried 36 dark pages of 174 before this wire (138 already lit, largely from the segments layer).
_receipts.record_url: dataset precision — no per-record URL column exists, matching the sibling.

_receipts.overlap_matrix_full_sets: Resolved on COMPLETE distinct-KeyNo sets, not samples. Distinct KeyNo: L0 464 · L1 229 · L2 742 · L3 977, each proven complete by a resultOffset==count re-query returning 0 features. Pairwise: L1⊂L0 (229 shared, 0 L1-only) · L2⊂L3 (742 shared, 0 L2-only) · L0∩L2 = 0 · L1∩L3 = 0 · L0∩L3 = 235. Three disjoint blocks: A=229 (lines only), B=235 (line AND point), C=742 (points only). Arithmetic closes exactly: L0=A+B=464, L1=A=229, L2=C=742, L3=B+C=977, and A+B+C=1,206 = |L0 ∪ L3| = |all four unioned|.

_receipts.layer_set: L0 ITSM STIP Point (point) 1,065 rows / 433 distinct project_id · L1 ITSM STIP Line (polyline) 706 rows / 356 distinct · L2 ITSM STIP ALL (point) 1,751 rows / 776 distinct.
_receipts.why_l2_not_wired: L2 'ALL' is NOT an independent layer and is NOT wired. Measured on COMPLETE distinct project_id sets (each proven complete by a resultOffset==count re-query returning 0 features): L1\L2 = 0, L2\(L0 ∪ L1) = 0, L0\L2 = 5, |L0 ∪ L1| = 781 = |all three unioned|. So L2 is exactly L0 ∪ L1 minus 5 point-only keys — it contributes nothing and wiring it alongside L0/L1 would multi-count nearly every project. The row-count arithmetic hinted at this (1,065 + 706 = 1,771 vs 1,751) but did NOT establish it; only the key sets did.
_receipts.yield_rationale: POINTS yields_to LINES. On the full sets L0 ∩ L1 = 8; on the wired forward subset it is 6. A polyline intersects many ZIP radii where a point sits in exactly one, so the line is the copy worth keeping. Same class as ID/OH/ME/VT/UT/IA/VA — omitting the yield double-emits the shared projects; NY is the counter-case where declaring one would have dropped records. Measured per source, never inherited.
_receipts.status_no_column: Neither layer has a status field (schemas are identical apart from Shape__Length on the polyline). status_const, the MT/ADOT STIP precedent, bucketed proposed.
_receipts.forward_window_and_why: extra_where 'drft_year >= 2026' — a DELIBERATE conservative restriction, not a recency filter. drft_year is an Integer fiscal year whose vocabulary is complete on both layers (L0 11 values summing exactly to 1,065, range 2020-2032; L1 11 values summing exactly to 706, range 2021-2032) and it INCLUDES PAST YEARS: 559 of L0's 1,065 rows are 2020-2025. Unlike Idaho's ITIP — where every ProgramYear was 2027+ so 'proposed' was provable — a 2020-programmed Wyoming project may well be built, and this service carries no evidence either way. Bucketing those 'proposed' would assert not-yet-built without evidence; bucketing them 'operating' would fabricate completion. They are therefore EXCLUDED rather than guessed. Cost of the choice, stated plainly: 544 distinct projects wired of 781 total (L0 256 + L1 294 forward keys, overlap 6).
_receipts.annual_maintenance: The 2026 literal in extra_where is a fixed year, so the forward window widens by one year every January. Revisit annually — or replace it if WYDOT ever publishes a real status column, which would make the restriction unnecessary.
_receipts.no_date_field: There is no esriFieldTypeDate field. drft_year is an Integer fiscal year, and ce11/con1 are cost estimate doubles (verified on sampled rows: ce11 160163.24, con1 2912058.76). So file_date/file_date_kind/recency_days are absent — the shape 33 other wired programmed-work entries already use. A bare year is never interpolated into a day.
_receipts.type_vocabulary: cow_desc. L0 = 46 values summing EXACTLY to 1,065 (45 non-null + a genuine NULL on 1 row, deliberately unmapped); L1 = 20 summing EXACTLY to 706. The union of 52 non-null values is mapped, so 0 unclassified on either layer. Roadway/structure/rail/ITS → Utility; airports, buildings, parking and transit rolling stock → Civic/Public; planning, studies, administration and land acquisition → Development, the closed vocabulary's generic member (never the off-vocabulary string 'Other').
_receipts.record_url: dataset precision — no per-record URL column exists, so the service layer URL is the machine URL (Boulder/Philadelphia precedent).
_receipts.coverage: district/route/wyo_route span the state, so coverage declares {state: WY} with no county, per the UDOT statewide precedent. Wyoming carried 91 dark pages of 103 before this wire.

arcgis._receipts: 2026-08-25 KY wire. KYTC's enacted Six-Year Highway Plan. SYPQuery = Project_Locations_Line JOINED to TED_CHIPS_ACTIVEPLAN; 43,361 rows unfiltered, 1,779 on the current plan. ORG IDENTITY VERIFIED BY NAME not acronym: service copyrightText 'KYTC', serviceDescription 'Highway Plan Projects service'; the companion AGO org CcI36Pduqd0OR4W9 is owned by 'KYTCGIS'. EDGE-REACHABLE 4/4 spaced (200 in 3,239 / 3,085 / 3,432 / 3,952 ms, {"count":43361} byte-identical every round, matching pg_net exactly). CONNECTOR QUERY SHAPE PROVEN LIVE before wiring: where=1=1 AND (...), spatial envelope, qualified outFields projection, outSR=4326, resultOffset paging - Louisville offset 0 returned 50 features / offset 2 returned 48 with the first DIST_ITEM shifted (5-10016.00 -> 5-10064.00), geometry paths present for featurePoint() centroiding. FULLY-QUALIFIED FIELD NAMES ARE MANDATORY: on a joined MapServer layer the short names do not exist, and querying them returns an HTTP 200 carrying {"error":{"code":400}} - the South Dakota class. readCol does plain row[ref] with no dot-path traversal (that is Socrata's feature), so dotted keys are safe here; verified in code before relying on it. VINTAGE GATE: the layer holds EVERY Highway Plan back to 1996 - PLANYEAR x CUR_PLANYEAR_IND enumerated complete, 16 biennial groups summing exactly to 18,683. extra_where CUR_PLANYEAR_IND='Y' is the PUBLISHER'S OWN current-plan flag; without it 1996 programme rows publish as live development. STATUS IS A COMPOSITE of Construction Stage + PRECONFLAG because NEITHER COLUMN ALONE IS CORRECT: PRECONFLAG alone mis-files 47 approved rows as proposed, STAGEC alone fails 72 rows closed on a null stage. The two-way crosstab was enumerated complete, all 18 combinations summing EXACTLY to 1,785, and every combination is mapped - so a new one fails closed and is named in unmapped_statuses. status_raw is DIAGNOSTIC ONLY, never rendered (lib/map.js renders the bucket), so the two-token key costs the resident nothing and makes the run report legible. Rejected/Withdrawn are excluded IN THE MAP rather than via extra_where so they show up in excluded_by_status instead of vanishing at source. CRITICAL - SYP_RPT_PRECONFLAG IS PRECON-SCOPED: 'I' MEANS PRECONSTRUCTION FINISHED, NOT PROJECT DEAD. An earlier draft proposed I -> exclude; that would have dropped 43 AWARDED construction contracts including the Covington/Newport 4th Street Bridge replacement (6-1086.00, authorized 2026-03-16) and the I-471 Ohio River bridge (6-10036.00). 43 of 57 I rows sit at construction stage AWARDED, all 57 carry a non-null construction authorized date, max construction FY 2031, and the explicit 'Awarded' flag holds only 4 rows. No written KYTC definition exists to confirm this on paper - every field carries domain:null - so the evidence is behavioural and is recorded here in full. TYPE_MAP: SYP_RPT_TYPEWORK enumerated complete on the current plan, 55 values summing EXACTLY to 1,785, including a literal 'UNKNOWN' (4 rows) mapped to the generic Development bucket rather than guessed (Phoenix rule). The vocabulary carries SUFFIXED AND UN-SUFFIXED DUPLICATES of the same work type (MAJOR WIDENING 24 vs MAJOR WIDENING(O) 46; RECONSTRUCTION 43 vs RECONSTRUCTION(O) 136) and a publisher typo (MINR WIDENING, 1) - all mapped verbatim, because mapping what the publisher emits is the contract. RECORD_URL IS DATASET PRECISION FOR A REASON, NOT A LIMITATION: PRECON_INFO_LINK is populated on 18,683 of 18,683 rows with a genuine per-record URL (pmtoolbox.kytc.ky.gov/SYPmapsPreconReport.asp?COMB=<DIST_ITEM>) and would be record precision - but that host serves an EXPIRED TLS CERTIFICATE, confirmed by two independent clients (pg_net 'SSL peer certificate or SSH remote key was not OK'; Deno 'invalid peer certificate: Expired'). The problem is AGENCY-WIDE, not one endpoint: datamart.kytc.ky.gov (KYTC's own SYP20detail.asp) fails identically. Shipping it would hand every Kentucky resident a browser certificate interstitial, so record_url is omitted from column_map and the ladder falls through to dataset_url. RE-PROBE BOTH HOSTS: the day KYTC renews, adding record_url + record precision is a ONE-LINE upgrade. dataset_url was chosen from VERIFIED candidates after four guessed URLs 404'd (maps.kytc.ky.gov/highwayplan/, /syp/, host root 406, transportation.ky.gov/.../Highway-Plan.aspx) - the Program Management page is the owning division's, 200 in 370 ms. COVERAGE PRE-VERIFIED on all 126 modelled KY ZIPs with the connector's own 3-mi envelope: 126/126 answered cleanly, 119 return >=1 current-plan project; 46 of the 51 DARK pages would light (337 records, avg 7, max 50), taking KY from 75 to 121 of 126 lit. Max 65 records on any page - no row-size concern. The 5 still dark: 40461, 41007, 42206, 42356, 42378. REJECTED IN THE SAME PASS with receipts: Apps/ProjectControl (its own description says Right-of-Way MONUMENTS and Project Control - survey control points, not projects); Apps/ProjectArchives (scanned project plans 1909-present - as-builts); SHIFT_2026_Statewide_Projects (40 rows, and SHIFT is the PRIORITISATION formula, not a programme); and the ActiveHighwayPlan_Ext_Prd FeatureServer's own layers 0/1/2, which are dynamic LRS layers that reject where=1=1 in EVERY form tried - and per the NDOT standing answer extra_where can never rescue a 1=1 failure, because buildWhere always prefixes the spatial clause 1=1 and ANDs after it.
